_link.title: I can explain pruning as a mechanism of synaptic plasticity

toLevel2.stem: What is pruning in the context of synaptic plasticity?
toLevel2.answer: The elimination of unused synaptic connections
distractors: The creation of new synaptic connections
The strengthening of existing connections
The duplication of active neural pathways

toLevel2.stem: Why does pruning occur at synaptic connections?
toLevel2.answer: The connections are not adequately activated
distractors: The connections are frequently activated
The connections are newly formed by sprouting
The connections carry too much information

toLevel2.stem: What does pruning enhance in the brain?
distractors: The total number of synaptic connections
The size of the dendrites on each neuron
The amount of neurotransmitter produced

toLevel2.stem: What happens to neural resources freed by pruning?
toLevel2.answer: They support stronger and more essential connections
distractors: They are permanently lost from the brain
They are stored for future neuron production
They are converted into neurotransmitter chemicals

toLevel2.stem: Which type of synaptic connections does pruning remove?
toLevel2.answer: Connections that are not regularly used
distractors: Connections that are frequently activated
Connections that were most recently formed
Connections that carry excitatory signals

toLevel2.stem: Pruning is the elimination of synaptic connections that are not adequately activated.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: Pruning increases the total number of synaptic connections in the brain.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: Pruning is the {{blank:1}} of synaptic connections that are not adequately activated.

distractors: strengthening
duplication

toLevel2.stem: Pruning enhances the {{blank:1}} of brain functioning by removing unused connections.

distractors: complexity
size

toLevel2.stem: When synaptic connections are not used, they are removed to accommodate {{blank:1}} and more essential connections.

distractors: weaker
newer

toLevel3.stem: Why is pruning considered adaptive rather than harmful?
toLevel3.answer: It frees resources for more frequently used connections
distractors: It permanently destroys important neural pathways
It prevents the brain from forming any new connections
It has no adaptive function and always impairs performance

toLevel3.stem: How does pruning contribute to the efficiency of brain functioning?
toLevel3.answer: By removing unused connections so resources support active pathways
distractors: By strengthening every connection regardless of how often it fires
By creating new neurons to replace the pruned synaptic connections
By increasing the number of receptor sites on all dendrites

toLevel3.stem: How does pruning relate to long-term depression?
toLevel3.answer: Pruning is the structural mechanism through which LTD weakens connections
distractors: Pruning and LTD are completely unrelated neural processes in the brain
Pruning strengthens connections while LTD weakens them simultaneously
LTD prevents pruning from occurring at any synaptic connection

toLevel3.stem: Why would a person who learnt recorder in primary school but stopped playing for 15 years find the skill harder to perform?
toLevel3.answer: The relevant synaptic connections were pruned due to disuse
distractors: The brain replaced recorder neurons with entirely new neurons
The synaptic connections were strengthened by long-term potentiation
The skill was never stored in synaptic connections in the first place

toLevel3.stem: How does pruning differ from sprouting as a mechanism of synaptic plasticity?
toLevel3.answer: Pruning removes connections; sprouting creates new ones
distractors: Both pruning and sprouting remove unused synaptic connections
Both pruning and sprouting create new synaptic connections
Pruning creates connections; sprouting removes unused ones

toLevel3.stem: Why does the brain prune connections rather than maintaining all of them?
toLevel3.answer: Maintaining unused connections wastes resources needed elsewhere
distractors: The brain cannot physically hold more than a fixed number of connections
Unused connections become toxic and must be removed for safety
Pruning occurs randomly and is not related to connection usage

toLevel3.stem: Pruning is adaptive because it frees neural resources for connections that are used more frequently.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: Pruning is the structural mechanism through which {{blank:1}} weakens synaptic connections over time.

distractors: LTP
sprouting

toLevel3.stem: A person who stopped playing recorder 15 years ago finds the skill harder because the relevant connections were {{blank:1}} due to disuse.

distractors: strengthened
duplicated

toLevel3.stem: Pruning removes connections, while {{blank:1}} creates new connections as mechanisms of synaptic plasticity.

distractors: pruning
rerouting

toLevel4.stem: Mia learnt to speak basic French in Year 7 but has not used it for eight years. She now struggles to recall vocabulary. Which process best explains this?
toLevel4.answer: Pruning eliminated the French-language synaptic connections due to disuse
distractors: LTP strengthened the French connections making them harder to access
New neurons replaced the French vocabulary with other subject content
The vocabulary was never stored in synaptic connections in her brain

toLevel4.stem: A VCE exam asks: 'Explain how pruning enhances brain efficiency.' Which response would earn full marks?
toLevel4.answer: Pruning removes unused connections so resources support more essential pathways
distractors: Pruning strengthens all existing connections to improve brain performance
Pruning creates new neurons that replace the connections being removed
Pruning increases the number of receptor sites on frequently used dendrites

toLevel4.stem: Jack played competitive tennis as a child but stopped at age 12. At age 25, he finds his technique has declined significantly. How does pruning explain this?
toLevel4.answer: Disuse caused the tennis-related synaptic connections to be eliminated
distractors: Frequent mental rehearsal strengthened irrelevant motor pathway connections
New neurons were created that overwrote his original tennis skill memories
His motor pathways were physically damaged by the absence of all practice

toLevel4.stem: A student writes: 'Pruning destroys neurons that are no longer needed.' How should this be corrected?
toLevel4.answer: Pruning eliminates synaptic connections, not the neurons themselves
distractors: The statement is correct and does not require any correction at all
Pruning destroys neurons and also eliminates all surrounding connections
Pruning only affects receptor sites and has no effect on connections

toLevel4.stem: A teacher asks students to link pruning to LTD. Which response correctly applies this relationship?
toLevel4.answer: Pruning is the structural change through which LTD weakens unused connections
distractors: Pruning and LTD are separate processes with no relationship to each other
Pruning causes LTP, which then produces the weakening effect of LTD
LTD prevents pruning from occurring by maintaining all existing connections

toLevel4.stem: Sophie learnt to knit in primary school but stopped practising for ten years. She now cannot remember the technique. A friend says this is because her brain is damaged. How should Sophie correct this?
toLevel4.answer: Pruning adaptively removed the unused knitting connections to free resources
distractors: Her friend is correct that brain damage is the only possible explanation
The knitting skill was never learned properly in the first place at all
Her brain replaced the knitting neurons with entirely different neurons

toLevel4.stem: A researcher examines brain tissue from a person who abandoned violin practice years ago. Which finding would be most consistent with pruning?
toLevel4.answer: Fewer synaptic connections in the relevant motor regions
distractors: Increased synaptic connections throughout the motor cortex areas
No structural changes of any kind in the relevant brain regions
Bushier dendrites and more receptor sites in the motor cortex

toLevel4.stem: Mia's inability to recall French vocabulary after eight years is explained by {{blank:1}}, which eliminated the relevant connections due to {{blank:2}}.

distractors: sprouting
potentiation
overuse
damage

toLevel4.stem: A student who writes that pruning 'destroys neurons' should correct this to say pruning eliminates synaptic {{blank:1}}, not the neurons themselves.

distractors: chemicals
vesicles

toLevel4.stem: Jack's decline in tennis technique is explained by pruning because {{blank:1}} caused the relevant motor connections to be eliminated.

distractors: practice
injury

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that pruning is harmful because it causes people to lose skills they once had. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; pruning is adaptive because it frees resources for essential connections
distractors: Correct; pruning is always harmful and serves no useful purpose at all
Correct; losing skills is always negative and pruning should be prevented
Incorrect; pruning does not cause any loss of skills under any circumstances

toLevel5.stem: Dr Nguyen argues that pruning and sprouting are opposite processes. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Correct; pruning removes connections while sprouting creates new ones
distractors: Incorrect; both processes remove unused synaptic connections from the brain
Incorrect; both processes create new synaptic connections in the brain
Correct; but only because sprouting reverses the specific connections pruning removed

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that pruning 'destroys neurons in the brain.' Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; pruning eliminates connections between neurons, not the neurons themselves
distractors: Correct; pruning completely destroys neurons that are no longer being used
Correct; the elimination of connections is the same as destroying the neurons
Incorrect; pruning actually strengthens neurons rather than affecting them

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that once pruning has occurred, the lost skill can never be relearned. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; resumed practice can trigger sprouting and LTP to rebuild connections
distractors: Correct; once connections are pruned they are permanently and irreversibly gone
Correct; the brain cannot form new connections in areas where pruning occurred
Incorrect; pruning does not affect skill retention in any way and is irrelevant

toLevel5.stem: A student suggests that preventing all pruning would improve brain performance. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; without pruning the brain would waste resources on unnecessary connections
distractors: Correct; preventing pruning would ensure all learned skills are retained forever
Correct; pruning serves no useful function and preventing it would be beneficial
Incorrect; but only because pruning cannot actually be prevented by any means

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that pruning only affects motor skills, not academic knowledge. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; pruning affects any synaptic connections that are not adequately activated
distractors: Correct; pruning is limited to motor skill pathways in the brain only
Correct; academic knowledge is stored differently and is immune to pruning
Incorrect; pruning only affects academic knowledge and not motor skills

toLevel5.stem: A textbook states that pruning 'cleans up the brain.' Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Acceptable metaphor; pruning removes unused connections to improve efficiency
distractors: Incorrect; pruning has no cleaning or organisational function in the brain
Correct; pruning literally removes waste material from inside the brain
Incorrect; pruning adds connections rather than removing any from the brain

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that pruning is the same as forgetting. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Oversimplified; pruning is one neural mechanism that contributes to forgetting
distractors: Correct; pruning and forgetting are identical interchangeable concepts always
Incorrect; pruning has no connection to forgetting or memory loss at all
Correct; there is no difference between the two terms in psychology

toLevel5.stem: The claim that pruning destroys neurons is {{blank:1}} because pruning eliminates {{blank:2}} between neurons, not the neurons themselves.

distractors: correct
plausible
chemicals
impulses

toLevel5.stem: The claim that a pruned skill can never be relearned is {{blank:1}} because resumed practice can trigger {{blank:2}} to rebuild the connections.

distractors: correct

pruning
